extracted.intended_audience: high-school and college students, teachers, and directors of school mathematical societies (including teachers of gifted students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and editorial standards for selecting, organizing, and presenting mathematical olympiad problems and solutions for use by students, teachers, and mathematical societies. Emphasizes problem difficulty, pedagogical use, and solution detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize originality over manipulative skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are 'unconventional' in that they 'stress originality of thought rather than mere manipulative ability' and 'introduce the necessity for finding new methods of attack.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and present problems that reward creative approaches and new ideas rather than routine algebraic manipulation or rote procedures. Favor problems that 'emphasize the creative aspects' of elementary mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete solutions with detail for difficult problems
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Complete solutions to all problems are given; in many cases, alternate solutions are detailed ... The solutions to more advanced problems are given in considerable detail.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full solutions for every problem; for harder problems, give especially detailed explanations and, where appropriate, alternate approaches to illuminate different viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give hints for every problem and mark difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Hints have been given for every problem, and those problems which to the authors appear of greater difficulty have been starred (*).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least one hint per problem to assist learning; use explicit markers (e.g., stars) to flag problems of greater difficulty so teachers and students can triage exercises by level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group problems by topical sections and supply preparatory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are grouped into twelve separate sections; 'Where more advanced concepts are employed, the concepts are discussed in the section preceding the problems, which gives the volume the aspect of a textbook as well as a problem book.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content into coherent topical sections; when problems require advanced or nonstandard concepts, include a short explanatory section ahead of the problems to make them accessible to the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience and difficulty range
rubrics_metrics.description: Most problems 'presuppose only high school mathematics' and are 'within reach of seventh- and eighth-grade students of outstanding ability,' but 'some are of uncommon difficulty' that may challenge research mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim problems primarily at able high-school students (US grades 9–12 equivalent), while including a range from introductory to exceptionally challenging to engage both younger gifted students and advanced learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer conceptual/creative problems over routine manipulative ones
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'special effort has been made to play down problems (particularly those in algebra) involving detailed manipulative matter' to avoid duplicating other algebra problem books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting problems, deprioritize exercises that are mainly mechanical algebraic manipulation; prefer problems that cultivate reasoning, insight, and novel techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for multiple educational contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: The book 'lends itself exceptionally well to use in the various Institutes for high school mathematics teachers' and 'is certainly required reading for teachers dealing with the gifted student and advanced placement classes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design problems/solutions so they can be used in math clubs, teacher training, advanced placement classes, self-study, and contest preparation; provide material adaptable to these settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality: revise to remove errors and improve solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The third Russian edition 'differs from the second chiefly in the elimination of errors detected in the second edition' and the second edition reworked problems and solutions (omitted ~60 problems, added ~120, restudied placements, reworked solutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an editorial process that corrects errors, improves or simplifies unclear proofs, reorganizes sections for better flow, and updates problem selection based on pedagogical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve fidelity to original sources and notations
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation 'was felt that the volume would lose something by too much tampering' and 'some notations which differ in minor respects from the standard American notations have been retained; these will cause no difficulty.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When translating or adapting original contest material, retain original structure, references, and reasonable notation to preserve the character and provenance of the problems, altering only to clarify or correct genuine errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document provenance and contest numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems largely 'first appeared in competitive examinations sponsored by the School Mathematical Society of the Moscow State University and in the Mathematical Olympiads held in Moscow' and a 'Numerical Reference to the Problems Given in the Moscow Mathematical Olympiads' is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the source and contest associations of problems (e.g., original contest numbers) to provide historical/provenance context and to help instructors select problems by contest origin or year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include supplementary references and theoretical material where useful
rubrics_metrics.description: The last four sections 'contain important theoretical material, and they may well serve as study topics'; 'supplementary references given in various sections will also prove useful.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment problem collections with concise theoretical background and bibliographic references in sections where deeper or less-standard concepts appear to support further study and teacher preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use problems to develop methods and original thinking, not rote answers
rubrics_metrics.description: The books are 'designed not only to reinforce the student's formal knowledge, but also to acquaint him with methods and ideas new to him and to develop his predilection for, and ability in, original thinking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame and select problems so that solving them requires learning or applying methods and fosters independent, original problem-solving habits rather than memorizing standard solutions.
